processing: Little is documented for this cultivar alone. Typical of Darjeeling, leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, with flush and maker shaping the style.
harvest_season: As with other Darjeeling teas, picking follows the flushes from spring into autumn; which flush suits this cultivar best is not well recorded.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, a mix of green, brown and silvery leaf that shifts darker in later flushes.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Darjeeling, pale gold to amber depending on the flush.
appearance_wet: Typical of Darjeeling, a mottled green and coppery leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for this cultivar on its own; as with other Darjeeling teas, expect floral and muscat-leaning notes that vary by flush.

brewing.notes: A general Darjeeling starting point. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for a green-leaning first flush.

vintage_note: Darjeeling teas are usually sold by the flush and year of the harvest, and often by garden and lot. A cultivar name like T78 appears only when the garden chooses to state it, so ask for the invoice details.
description:
T78 is the name of a tea cultivar listed for Darjeeling. Beyond the name, little is documented about it.

What ends up in the cup depends on the usual Darjeeling variables: flush, garden and how the maker handled the leaf. As with other Darjeeling teas, those can matter as much as the plant itself.

Brew it the way you would any Darjeeling of the same flush, and taste before judging by the label. If a lot names T78, ask the seller which garden and picking it comes from, as that is the most useful thing to know.
history: Little is documented about who selected T78, when, or how widely it is planted. Its association with Darjeeling is about all that can be said with confidence.
